suffisaunt.def: In the best instruments, the Almicanteras, or circles of altitude, were drawn at distances of one degree only; in less-carefully made instruments, they were drawn at distances of two degrees. The one given to his son by Chaucer was one of the latter

latitude-t.gloss: the distance of any place on the globe, N. or S. of the equator

latitude-a.gloss: the angular distance of any body from the ecliptic
latitude-a.def: the angular distance of any body from the ecliptic, measured along a great circle at right angles to the ecliptic

conclusions.def: mathematical propositions, either problems or theorems

certein.def: a certein, i.e. a certain number; but the word nombre need not be repeated

bihestes.def: promises, i. e. what they profess to prove

con.def: To con one thanks, Fr. savoir gre, to feel thankful and make the feeling known to the object of it.

altitude.gloss: the elevation of a celestial object above the horizon
altitude.def: the elevation of a celestial object above the horizon, measured along a vertical arc

meridian.def: meridional, at the moment of southing, exact southern

kalendres.def: The old calendars answered nearly to our modern almanacks.

somer.def: The Kalendar of John Somer is extant in MS. Cotton, Vesp. E. vii. It is calculated for 140 years from 1367

lenne.def: Nicolaus de Lynna, i.e. of Lynn, in Norfolk, was a noted astrologer in the reign of Edward III., and was himself a writer of a treatise on the Astrolabe.

zodiac.def: An imaginary belt in the heavens, of the breadth of 12°, along the middle of which runs the ecliptic.

ecliptik.def: A great circle of the sphere, drawn along the middle of the zodiac, making an angle with the equator of about 23°. 28'; the apparent path of the sun, nearly.

equacions.def: The " equations of houses " means the method of dividing the sphere equally into "houses" for astrological purposes

houses.def: The whole celestial sphere was divided into twelve equal portions, called houses, by six great circles passing through the north and south points of the horizon

dignetes.def: the advantages which a planet has on account of being in a particular place in the zodiac, or in such a station with other planets

ref.head: Vouche
ocrFixes: Youclie, V. to vouch → Vouche, v. to vouch

rewle.gloss: the revolving long and narrow plate or rod used for measuring and taking altitudes

ref.head: Rewle
ocrFixes: long and 2l6 narrow → long and narrow

rewle.def: At the back of the astrolabe revolved the 'rule,' made of metal, and fitted with sights

maner.def: used without of following, as maner turet, kind of " turet,"

turet.gloss: the eye in which the ring of the Astrolabe turned
turet.def: It seems to mean both a ring which turns round, and an eye in which a ring can turn.

moder.def: the thickest plate forming the body or principal part of the Astrolabe

ocrFixes: Resseyuy th, jj>r. s. → Resseyuyth, pr. s.

wombe.gloss: the depression in the front of an astrolabe

clymatz.gloss: climates, i. e. zones of latitude
clymatz.def: sometimes an instrument was provided with several of them, differently marked, for use in places having different latitudes

riet.def: The 'rete' or 'net' is the circular plate with many openings which revolves within the 'mother.'

bakhalf.gloss: the back or flat side of the astrolabe

over-thwart.gloss: exactly across, at right angles to

croos-lyne.gloss: cross-line, the line from right to left through the centre in Fig. 1

mile-wey.def: a space of 5°, which answers to twenty minutes of time, the average time for walking a mile ; hence the term

minute-d.gloss: a sixtieth part of a degree

scale.def: scale, or rather, double scale, for measuring both by U7nbra recta and umbra versa

umbra-v.gloss: the upper part of the same, or the part perpendicular to the 'crossline,'

pyn.gloss: the pin which passes through the central hole in the Astrolabe and its plates

clymates.gloss: sets of almicanteras calculated for various terrestrial latitudes
clymates.line: sets of almicanteras calculated for various terrestrial latitudes

hors.def: a name for the little wedge that passes through a hole in the end of the "pyn,"

equinoxial.def: said of the equinoctial circle or equator, the great circle of the sphere whose poles are the arctic and antarctic poles

heved-s.gloss: head; the beginning or first point of a zodiacal sign

hedes.gloss: heads, or first points of signs

solsticioun.gloss: the solstice, or point of the ecliptic most remote from the equator

tropik.gloss: the turning-point, a name for the solstitial points

tropos.gloss: a turning ; but interpreted by Chaucer to mean "agaynward," i. e. backward

agaynward.gloss: backward, at the point of return

weyere.def: a translation of the Lat. equator, because it weighs equally the night and day ; i. e. the days and nights, at the equinoxes, are equal

girdel.gloss: girdle, cincture, central line or great circle

almicanteras.gloss: small circles of declination (in the celestial sphere)

senith.gloss: the zenith, or visible pole of the horizon

calle.gloss: caul, a net used to confine women's hair

kerving.gloss: carving, i. e. cutting, crossing over

costes.gloss: coasts, directions, i. e. parts of the sky to be observed

cenith.gloss: a word denoting the point where a given azimuth-circle meets the horizon

longitudes.def: The longitude of a star is measured along the ecliptic; that of a town, from a fixed meridian.

centre-r.gloss: the "centre" or small point at the very end of which is the position of a fixed star in the Rete of the Astrolabe

lyne-right.gloss: in an exact line, exactly in a line with

superfice-n.gloss: closely bordering upon, in the immediate neighbourhood of

bestes.gloss: the "beasts" or animals in the zodiacal signs

label.gloss: the narrow revolving rod or rule on the front of the astrolabe

almury.gloss: the 'denticle' or tooth-like point or pointer situate on the Rete near the 'head' of Capricorn

ref.head: Almury
ocrFixes: the ' denticle ' or tooth like → the 'denticle' or tooth-like

assendent.def: The 'ascendant' is that degree of the ecliptic which is rising above the horizon at a given moment.

aspecte.def: An 'aspect' is the angular distance between two planets. The principal aspects are five, viz. conjunction, sextile, quartile, trine, and opposition, corresponding to the angular distances 0°, 60°, 90°, 120°, and 180°, respectively.

combust.def: quenched, viz. by being so near the sun as to be obscured by his superior light

descencioun.def: The technical signification seems to be — the "house" or portion of the sky just above the western horizon, so that perhaps a planet in his descension is about to set. (?)

dignitee.def: Dignity, in astrology, signifies the advantages which a planet has when in a particular position in the zodiac, or in a particular position with regard to other planets

dragoun-tail.def: the point where a planet (esp. the moon) passed from the northern to the southern side of the ecliptic. (The opposite node was called the Dragon's Head.)

face-a.gloss: a portion of the zodiac 10 degrees long

horoscopo.gloss: within that part of the sky considered as the ascendent
horoscopo.line: within that part of the sky considered as the ascendent

hous.gloss: a 'house' or portion of the sky (in astrology)

ref.head: Hous
ocrFixes: a ' house' or portion of the sky (in astrologjO → a 'house' or portion of the sky (in astrology)

hous.def: The whole celestial sphere was divided into twelve equal portions

ioigned.gloss: joined, nearly or altogether in conjunction

iudicial.def: Judicial astrology pretended to forecast the destinies of men and nations ; natural astrology foretold natural events, such as the weather and seasons.

nativitez.gloss: nativities, castings of nativity in astrology

resceived.gloss: favourably situated with respect to 'other planets

retrograd.gloss: moving in a direction contrary to that of the sun's motion in the ecliptic

shrewe.gloss: evil planet, planet of evil influence

succedent.def: The succedent houses are the second, fifth, eighth, and eleventh, as these are about to follow the most important houses

prikke-m.gloss: a small mark, such as a little stick stuck in the ground

nadir.gloss: the point of the ecliptic exactly opposite to that in which the sun is situate

ark.gloss: arc, the angular distance apparently passed over by the sun during a day or a night

latitude-c.gloss: the breadth of a climate, or a line along which such breadth is measured

longitude-m.gloss: the distance between two given meridians

longitude-c.gloss: the length or extent of a ' climate,' in a direction parallel to the equator

inequales.def: hours formed by dividing the duration of daylight by twelve

arch.def: the angular distance apparently passed over by the sun during a day or a night

artificial.def: The day artificial is the length of the day, from the moment of sunrise to that of sunset.

vulgar.def: The day vulgar is the length of the "artificial" day, with the durations of morning and evening twilight added to it.

naturaly.def: A 'day natural' is a period of 24 hours, as distinct from the 'day artificial.'

any-thing.gloss: in any degree, at all, to any appreciable extent

declinacion.gloss: the angular distance of a celestial object N. or S. of the equator
declinacion.def: the angular distance of a celestial object N. or S. of the equator, measured along an arc at right angles to it

declynen.def: possess declination, i. e. pass either to the north or south of the ecliptic

strange.def: Every star has its own degrees in the equator and ecliptic, viz. the degrees in which a great circle passing through the star and through the N. and S. poles cuts these circles respectively.

table.gloss: one of the thin plates on which almicanteras are engraved

elevacioun.gloss: the altitude above the horizon of the north pole

perche.gloss: a rod placed high up in a horizontal position

depressioun.gloss: the angular distance of the southern pole from the horizon

orison-rectum.def: This means the horizon of any place situate on the equator, which could be represented by a straight line upon a disc

tables-t.def: "Tables [in the last sense] be made of leues of yuery, boxe, cyprus, & other stouffe, daubed with waxe to wrytte on;" Hormani Vulgaria, leaf 81.

obedient.def: A technical term, applied to the eastern signs of the zodiac, as being respectively correspondent to the western ones.

sovereyn.def: A technical term, applied to the western signs of the zodiac, as superior to the "obedient" eastern ones.

tortuos.def: applied to the six signs of the zodiac (Capricorn to Gemini), which ascend most rapidly and obliquely

couching.gloss: laying down, letting the Astrolabe lie flat on the ground

sadly.gloss: carefully, steadily, with as little movement as possible

slely.gloss: slily, i. e. with great sleight or skill, skilfully

wey-s.gloss: the sun's apparent way or path during a given day

coniunccion.def: It means a very close apparent approach of two celestial bodies.

directe.def: A planet's motion is direct when it moves in the same direction as the sun along the signs.

episicle.def: A small circle, the centre of which moves along the circumference of a larger one.

house-a.gloss: a 'house' or portion of the sky (in astrology)

ref.head: Hous
ocrFixes: a ' house' or portion of the sky (in astrologjO → a 'house' or portion of the sky (in astrology)

heer-mele.gloss: the thickness of a hair, a hair's breadth

level.gloss: level (for ascertaining that a thing is level)

ony-thing.gloss: in any degree, at all, to any appreciable extent

stok.gloss: a stump or block of wood

clymat.gloss: a belt or zone of the earth included between two given lines of latitude
clymat.short: a belt or zone of the earth

illike-distant.gloss: at an even distance, i. e. parallel
illike-distant.def: {Not equidistant, because the climates varied in breadth.)

ref.head: Peyre
ocrFixes: a " pair," a set → a "pair," a set

peyre.def: A pair by no means implies that the set of similar things to which it is applied is limited to two.

vmbra-v.gloss: the upper part of the same, or the part perpendicular to the 'crossline,'

anni-c.def: When a table contains quantities denoting the amount of a planet's motion during round periods of years, such as 20, 40, or 60 years, such a change is entered under the heading Anni Collecti.

anni-e.def: When a table contains quantities denoting the amount of a planet's motion during only a few years, viz. from 1 to 20 years, such changes are entered separately under the headings 1, 2, 3, &c. years, which are designated the expanse (or separate) years.

anni-ce.gloss: the collected years and expanse years
anni-ce.line: the collected years and expanse years

annis-ce.gloss: the collected years and expanse years
annis-ce.line: the collected years and expanse years

entere.def: To 'enter with' is to keep in mind and search for, as a help to finding something else.

ref.head: Entere
ocrFixes: set down in writmg → set down in writing

mote.def: The "mene mote" or mean motion is the motion of a planet during a given period as stated in the tables.

rote.def: the tabulated quantity belonging to a given fixed date, from which corresponding quantities for other dates can be calculated by addition or subtraction
